findings.title: SendGrid client is never authenticated in the cron route, so the new cancellation calls fail silently
findings.body: This module only calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` (line 19); the `@sendgrid/client` default export used by the new cancellation block (`client.request` POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends at line 57) is never given an API key here. `sgMail` uses its own internal client instance, so setting the key on sgMail does not configure the exported `client` singleton, and in a per-route/serverless deployment the `client.setApiKey()` done at module load in emailReminderManager.ts does not apply to this route's module instance. The cancellation requests will go out without a valid Authorization header and fail (401); the surrounding try/catch only logs the error, so no reminders are actually cancelled and the bug this PR fixes silently persists. (The pre-existing `/v3/mail/batch` call at line 188 in the same file has the same problem.) Add `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` next to the sgMail one.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders and poisons every future cron run
findings.body: The new cancellation block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single try/catch. If `client.request` throws for any one reminder (e.g., SendGrid returns 404 for an unknown/expired batch_id, a transient 5xx, or a rate limit), every reminder after it in the list is skipped for that run, and the collected `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` promises are never executed — Prisma promises are lazy and only run when awaited, and the `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` after the loop is skipped when the loop throws. Because the failing row is never deleted or otherwise marked as handled, it is re-fetched on the next cron run 15 minutes later and aborts the loop again. A single persistently failing reminder can therefore block all cancellations indefinitely, so reminder emails for cancelled bookings keep being sent — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix. Each iteration (SendGrid cancel + row delete) needs its own try/catch so one failure doesn't poison the batch.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation calls are fire-and-forget; the cancelled flag may never be written before the response is returned
findings.body: The per-reminder cancellation calls (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` here and the SMS equivalent) are invoked inside `forEach` without await and their promises are never collected. The DB update that sets `cancelled: true` — the flag the cron job relies on to actually cancel the SendGrid send — is therefore not guaranteed to complete before the API handler returns; on serverless platforms the invocation can be frozen once the response is sent, the flag is never written, and the reminder email is still sent. The pre-change code awaited the reminder row deletions via `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(remindersToDelete))`; the new code awaits nothing reminder-related. The same un-awaited pattern exists in handleNewBooking.ts (reschedule path, ~line 968), trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx requestReschedule (~line 490) and trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx (~lines 214, 378, 521, 576). Collect these promises and await them (with per-item error handling) before returning.

findings.title: immediateDelete path cancels in SendGrid immediately and leaves stale rows, re-introducing the 100-pending-cancellations root cause
findings.body: The new `immediateDelete` branch of `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` cancels the SendGrid scheduled send right away but neither deletes the WorkflowReminder row nor sets `cancelled`, and it is used by the reschedule flow (handleNewBooking.ts line 968) and by workflow/step deletion (workflows.tsx lines 214 and 521). Cancelling immediately re-creates the root cause described in this PR: SendGrid keeps each pending cancellation until the original send date and caps pending cancellations at 100, so a burst of reschedules or workflow edits/deletions can exhaust the quota — after which the cron's deferred cancellations also start failing and cancelled-booking reminder emails go out again. Additionally the leftover row (scheduled=true, cancelled=null) lingers until the cron's past-date cleanup removes it, and if the same booking is cancelled later the same batch_id gets cancelled a second time. These paths should either use the deferred `cancelled` flag like the cancel-booking path, or delete the row after the immediate cancel.

findings.title: WorkflowReminder row is left behind when Twilio cancellation fails
findings.body: In `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, the row delete happens after `await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` inside the same try block; if the Twilio call throws, execution jumps to the catch and the WorkflowReminder row is never deleted. Unlike email reminders, no cron cleanup ever deletes SMS-method rows, so the stale row (scheduled=true) stays in the database indefinitely. Previously the callers deleted reminder rows in a separate awaited deleteMany regardless of the Twilio outcome. Delete the row in a finally block (or otherwise independently of the Twilio call's success).

findings.title: No tests cover the new cancel-flag and deferred cron cancellation flow
findings.body: The PR reworks reminder cancellation end to end (new `cancelled` column, flag-on-cancel instead of immediate SendGrid cancellation, cron-based cancellation within a 1-hour window, immediate cancellation for the reschedule and workflow-delete paths) but adds no tests for any of it: nothing verifies that cancelling a booking flags its email reminders and removes unscheduled ones, that the cron cancels and deletes flagged reminders inside the window while leaving later ones alone, or that the reschedule path cancels the old booking's reminders. The previous fix for this same bug (#6991) was wrong and shipped to production; without regression coverage on this flow the same class of bug can ship again.
